title: How Microsegmentation flow-based policy recommendations are generated, organized and accepted

prose.label: Related.
prose.text: Policies are in [[zms.policies]] and the Application Map entry point in [[zms.dashboards]]. What monthly or quarterly flows do to a recommendation is open in [[zms.overview]].

checks.do: Whether the recommendation shows a port conflict or a policy conflict before expecting to accept it.
The route from the Application Map resource group drawer to the recommendations page.

basis-14d.statement: Policy recommendations for resource groups are based on historical network flows, specifically flows observed within the past 14 days.

quotes: Microsegmentation provides policy recommendations for resource groups based on historical network flows.
Policy recommendations are generated based on flows observed within the past 14 days.
Review policy recommendations for a resource group based on flows from the last 14 days.

organization.statement: Recommendations are organized by managed and unmanaged flows, filterable by inbound or outbound direction.

quotes: organized by managed and unmanaged flows. You can filter managed and unmanaged flows by direction (i.e., inbound and outbound).

conflict-types.statement: A recommendation can have a port conflict (port not mapped to an Application Catalog application) and a policy conflict (source and destination resource groups already used in an existing policy); both must be resolved before it can be accepted.

quotes: Policy recommendations can have two types of conflicts—port conflicts and policy conflicts—that you must resolve in order to accept the recommendation and apply the policy.
A port conflict means the port is not mapped to an application in the Application Catalog and must be defined in the recommended policy.
A policy conflict means the source and destination resource groups in the recommended policy are used in an existing policy.

conflict-resolution.statement: A port conflict is resolved by choosing an Application Catalog application or adding the port as a manual port; a policy conflict is resolved by creating a new policy or merging into the existing one.

quotes: On the Port Conflicts tab, select the application from the Application Catalog that should be used by the port for the policy, or optionally add the port as a manual port, resolving the overlap.
You can either create the recommended policy as a new policy or merge it into an existing policy.

accept-toggle.statement: The Accept toggle is enabled when a recommendation has no conflicts, and such a recommendation can be accepted as is.

quotes: If the policy recommendation has no conflicts, the Accept toggle is enabled.
you can review and accept a recommendation as is, quickly applying the new policy and protecting flows.

listing-path.statement: Both articles give the same route to a resource group's recommendations: from Zero Trust Cloud > Dashboard > Microsegmentation Application Map, select a resource group and click Review Recommended Policies in its drawer, which opens the policy recommendations page for the resource group.

quotes: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Cloud > Dashboard > Microsegmentation Application Map.
On the Application Map, configure the filters as desired, then select a resource group.
In the drawer, click Review Recommended Policies.
The Policy Recommendation page for the resource group appears.
From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Cloud > Dashboard > Microsegmentation Application Map.
On the Application Map, configure the filters as needed, then select a resource group.
In the drawer, click Review Recommended Policies.
The policy recommendations page for the resource group appears.
